cues.text: Professor Tomlinson, may Annie and I please  quickly  ask  you  a  few questions about the reﬂective journal assignment?
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: It’s just that we’re a bit confused as to what you want us to include and discuss.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: Yes of course, what are you having trouble with?
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: Well, everything really. To start with, what should be included ﬁrst in the reflective journal?
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Perhaps suggestions from others?
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: No no, ﬁrstly you should include the study goals you set yourself at the beginning of the module.
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: This section should have been discussed in some detail towards the beginning of the course by Professor May.
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: You should be able to find her suggestions on the slides she has provided the class online.
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: Okay, thank you, Professor. Could I also trouble you to take a brief look at  my bibliography and footnotes?
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: I feel like they’re missing something; most of our friends’ bibliographies are longer.
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Well, looking at this Annie, I can see that you have used a wide range of resources, which shows that you have made eﬀective use of communication technology.
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: As far as I can tell, you need not make any changes to this, although you might want to double check that your referencing complies with the Harvard Referencing Style regulations.
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: Oh I’m very surprised you’ve said that! Thank you, now I can set my mind  at ease.
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Tom, you said you wanted to ask the Professor about the achievements section?
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Ah yes, Professor, in the assignment guidelines, we are asked to introduce and elaborate on our biggest achievement in the past, saying which skills we learnt in the process, and how these skills can  be  transferred  to  various  diﬀerent  future careers.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: The only problem is that I don’t know what my greatest  achievement actually is.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: I’ve only ever worked as a waiter in a hotel restaurant during the summer holidays from university.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: If you worked as a waiter in a hotel restaurant, you’re bound to have worked with other waiters as part of a team.
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: Would you say that during your time as a waiter, you developed any leadership skills?
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: Yes, well I suppose I was asked to become the team leader of the food and beverage department.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: But that’s hardly an achievement.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: You might not think so, but if you write that you were oﬀered the position of the team leader,
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: it shows a lot more about your character, for example that you’re charismatic and work well in a high-pressure situation.
cues.speaker: Prof. Tomlinson

cues.text: I never would have thought to write that down, thank you!
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: I guess I should start listening to others more often!
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: Annie, do you have any more questions or are you ready to go back to the library?
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: Yeah, I think I’ve got everything I need. Thank you very much, Professor Tomlinson!
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: That was really helpful.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: I’m actually starting to look forward to writing this now, and it should be a really useful exercise to prepare us for writing CVs and applying for jobs.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: It’s shocking how bad I am at identifying my strengths and weaknesses.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: Professor Tomlinson has shown me that I deﬁnitely need to start displaying some self-awareness!
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: Yeah, Tom,  you really do. You’re always so modest!
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Modesty is great until it comes to applying for jobs!
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Oh no! I forgot to ask the professor about the section on identifying the  skills gained through diﬀerent activities, do you remember?
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: When it asks you, for example, whether writing an essay develops your study skills or your independent learning and so on?
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Oh goodness, we really should have asked  him that. I’ve been having   trouble with it too.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: It just seems like such a pointless task. What do you reckon the answers are?
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: Hmm...I think writing an essay might be a way of identifying and resolving a problem, because you have to state the problem in the introduction and then solve it.
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: I’m not so sure about taking exams... I thought they were supposed to develop lots of diﬀerent skill sets.
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: If I really had to choose Q28 , I’d say that    taking exams enables you to become more confident in yourself.. .do you agree?
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: Maybe, I really don’t know either.
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: What do you think about the last two? Making class notes and presentation notes?
cues.speaker: Tom

cues.text: Oh it’s so diﬃcult! Q29 I think making class notes has to be a way of becoming a more independent learner because you yourself decide what the important information is and learn it.
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: That reminds me, Q30 I ﬁnd taking presentation notes is a disaster!
cues.speaker: Annie

cues.text: The professors speak much too quickly, and I write much too slowly,
cues.speaker: Annie
